theorem_title: Preservation of a physical frontier slot
natural_language_statement:
Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be finite types with decidable equality, $I$ a finite raw-incidence set over them with parameters $h,J$, and $w$ a wanted label. Let $\mu,\nu$ be integer memories and $b,c,k,s\in\mathbb N$ be base, capacity, depth and preservation boundary. Suppose the exact frontier-slot contract holds in $\mu$, the frontier length at $k$ is at most $c$, the next slot address is at most $s$, and the memories agree below $s$. Then

$$\operatorname{At}(\mu,I,w,b,c,k)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{At}(\nu,I,w,b,c,k).$$

This preserves the exact stored frontier count, query mask and aligned endpoint arrays through later scratch computation.
